This is the story of Dorothy. Her mother and
father died when she was very young, and she went
to live with Uncle Henry and Aunt Em in Kansas.
Kansas was often very windy. When the big winds
blew, the family always went into a hole under the

floor.

One day Uncle Henry stood at the door and looked
out at the gray sky.

“There's a big wind coming, Em,” he said to his
wife. “I’m going to look after the animals. Take

Dorothy into the hole, quickly.”

under the bed. Toto was her little black dog.
Dorothy tried to catch him. Aunt Em climbed down

to Dorothy to come. But the wind blew very hard
against the house and Dorothy fell on the floor, with

Toto in her arms.

“This isn’t Kansas!” she said to Toto. “Where are
we?”

She saw green grass and beautiful flowers, a river
and tall fruit trees.

“And who are these little people?” thought
Dorothy.

They were small, about as tall as she was, and all
their clothes were blue. An old woman spoke to
Dorothy.

“We are glad to see you, good witch, in the coun-
try of the Munchkins. You have killed the Wicked
Witch of the East!”

Dorothy and Toto soon found the yellow brick
road and walked along it, past the green fie) gs and
the blue Munchkin houses.

After a few miles Dorothy stopped and sat down
ona fence beside the road. Behind the fence was a
big field, and in it was a scarecrow on a stick, to
keep the birds away. Its head was a small bag, with

a Munchkin's hat on top. Toto saw it and barked.

“Good day,” said the Scarecrow. “How are you?”

“Very well, thank you,” said Dorothy. “How are
you?”

“Not very well. I don't like this stick. Please take
it away.”

Dorothy took the poor Scarecrow off the stick.

chapters.storyText:
One day, Dorothy caught her foot on something,
and one of the silver shoes came off. The Wicked
Witch at once picked it up and put it on her ugly
foot.

“Give that back to me!” said Dorothy.

“No,” said the Wicked Witch. “It’s mine now!”

Key Worps

“You wicked old witch!” cried Dorothy. Quickly
she picked up a pot of water and threw it over the
Witch.

“Help!” cried the Witch. “Water will kill me!”

Soon there was nothing of her. There was only one
silver shoe on the floor. Dorothy picked it up,
washed and dried it, and put it on again. Then she

ran to open the Lion’s door.

59

Dorothy and the Lion called the Winkies and said,
“The Witch is dead. Now please help us to find the
Tin Man and the Scarecrow.”

The Winkies found the broken Tin Man. Then
twenty of them worked day and night to put him
right. Soon he got up and did a little dance.

“I’m as good as new!” he said. “Now let’s find
the Scarecrow.”

The Winkies found the Scarecrow’s clothes at the
top of the tall tree. The Tin Man cut it down. The
Winkies filled the clothes with new straw, and soon
the Scarecrow was as good as new.

Now Dorothy and her friends spent a few happy
days at the castle. But one day Dorothy thought
about her aunt and uncle in Kansas.

“Oh, dear,” she said, “I do want to go home!”

“And I want a heart!” “And I want brains!” “And

1 want courage!”

Oz climbed into the basket and shouted, “While |
am away, I want the Scarecrow to be your king.”

He turned to Dorothy, “Jump in now!”

“I can’t find Toto anywhere,” said Dorothy. “I
can’t leave him behind.”

At last she found him. She picked him up and ran
to the balloon. Too late! It was already up in the

air.

“Take me with you!” she cried.

“I can't, my dear,” called Oz from the basket.
“Good-bye!”

And that was the last anybody ever saw of the
Wonderful Wizard of Oz. But the people of the
Emerald City said, “He was always our friend. Now

we have King Scarecrow, with his first-class brains!”
